intent.raw_query: Tokyo city break, $3000 for couple, food and tech culture, April 2026 from SFO

experiences.name: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore the bustling Tsukiji Outer Market, sampling fresh sushi, tamagoyaki, grilled seafood skewers, and matcha treats from local vendors. Engage with longtime vendors and discover the heart of Tokyo's culinary culture in one of the world's most famous food markets.

experiences.name: Akihabara Electric Town Tech & Anime Immersion
experiences.description: Dive deep into Tokyo's legendary tech and otaku culture in Akihabara. Browse multi-story electronics shops, retro game arcades, robot cafes, and cutting-edge gadget stores. Visit Yodobashi Camera and independent shops selling rare components, vintage consoles, and the latest tech innovations.

experiences.name: Ramen Alley Crawl in Shinjuku
experiences.description: Navigate the narrow lanes of Shinjuku's famous Omoide Yokocho (Memory Lane) and nearby ramen shops to taste regional ramen styles including tonkotsu, shoyu, and miso. Chat with ramen masters who have perfected their broths over decades and experience the authentic izakaya atmosphere.

experiences.name: teamLab Borderless Digital Art Museum
experiences.description: Experience the world-renowned teamLab Borderless, an immersive digital art museum that blends technology, art, and nature into breathtaking interactive installations. Wander through rooms of flowing light, digital waterfalls, and AI-driven environments that respond to your movement — a perfect fusion of tech culture and creativity.

experiences.name: Depachika Gourmet Basement Food Hall Experience
experiences.description: Descend into the legendary basement food halls (depachika) of Isetan or Takashimaya department stores in Shinjuku. Sample artisan wagashi sweets, premium bento boxes, regional Japanese delicacies, and gourmet street food prepared by top chefs. A uniquely Japanese culinary institution that reflects the country's obsession with food quality and presentation.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Tokyo
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Flight in transit
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A - Flight in transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Haneda/Narita Airport at 22:30. Clear customs and immigration, pick up a prepaid IC card (Suica or Pasmo) at the airport for budget-friendly transit. Take the airport limousine bus or train to your hotel area. Check in to Aegean Bliss Resort and settle in.

meals.breakfast: N/A - on flight
meals.lunch: N/A - on flight
meals.dinner: Grab a quick and cheap meal at the airport convenience store (7-Eleven or FamilyMart) — onigiri, sandwiches, and hot foods for under ¥600

day_by_day.notes: Keep energy low tonight — long travel day. Confirm your IC card is charged with at least ¥2,000 for the next few days. Convenience stores in Japan are excellent and very budget-friendly.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recover from jet lag. Late breakfast at the hotel or nearby convenience store. Take a slow walk around the local neighborhood to get oriented and find your nearest train station.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Akihabara — Tokyo's legendary electric town and tech culture hub. Explore multi-floor electronics shops like Yodobashi Camera and BIC Camera (free to browse). Visit retro game shops, anime figure stores, and gadget stalls. Many stores have free-to-explore floors with cutting-edge tech demos.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Akihabara's evening neon atmosphere. Walk the main street and check out maid cafes from the outside or try one for a unique cultural experience (budget around ¥1,500–¥2,000 for entry + drink).

meals.breakfast: Convenience store breakfast — onigiri + coffee for ¥400
meals.lunch: Akihabara ramen shop — try a bowl of tonkotsu or shoyu ramen for ¥700–¥900
meals.dinner: Yoshinoya or Matsuya gyudon (beef bowl) chain near Akihabara — filling meal for ¥500–¥700

day_by_day.notes: Akihabara is extremely walkable once you arrive by train. Use your IC card for the subway. Free Wi-Fi is available at most electronics stores.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Tsukiji Outer Market (free to explore) — the world-famous seafood and food market. Arrive early (by 8:00 AM) for the freshest experience. Sample tamagoyaki (egg rolls), fresh sushi, and street snacks while walking the stalls.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to nearby Hamarikyu Gardens (¥300 entry) — a beautiful traditional Japanese garden with a tidal pond. Then stroll along the Sumida River waterfront for free scenic views and people-watching.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Shiodome or Ginza area for evening window shopping. Visit the free observation deck at the Caretta Shiodome shopping complex for city views. Explore Ginza's illuminated streets at night — all free.

meals.breakfast: Tsukiji Outer Market breakfast — fresh tuna sushi set or tamagoyaki skewer for ¥800–¥1,200
meals.lunch: Tsukiji market stall lunch — sashimi bowl (kaisendon) for ¥1,000–¥1,500
meals.dinner: Conveyor belt sushi (kaiten-zushi) near Ginza — budget around ¥1,000–¥1,500 for a satisfying meal

day_by_day.notes: Tsukiji Outer Market is free to walk through. Arrive before 9:00 AM for the best selection. Many stalls close by early afternoon.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Senso-ji Temple in Asakusa — Tokyo's oldest and most iconic Buddhist temple (free entry). Arrive early to avoid crowds. Walk the Nakamise shopping street for traditional snacks and souvenirs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Asakusa neighborhood on foot — browse the Kappabashi Kitchen Town (free) where you can see realistic plastic food models and professional kitchen equipment. Cross the Azuma Bridge for views of the Tokyo Skytree.
day_by_day.evening: Take the train to Ueno and explore Ameyoko Market — a lively outdoor market street with cheap street food, clothing, and goods. Great for budget shopping and local food sampling.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store or hotel — ¥400
meals.lunch: Asakusa local tempura restaurant — tempura teishoku set meal for ¥900–¥1,200
meals.dinner: Ameyoko Market street food — yakitori skewers, gyoza, and beer for ¥800–¥1,200

day_by_day.notes: Senso-ji is free to enter. The 5-story pagoda and main hall are stunning especially in early morning light. April may still have cherry blossom remnants in Ueno Park nearby.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Odaiba — Tokyo's futuristic waterfront island with tech and innovation culture. Start with the free teamLab Borderless digital art museum exterior and the surrounding plaza. Explore the futuristic architecture and the life-sized Gundam statue (free to view).
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit DiverCity Tokyo Plaza (free to browse) and the nearby Palette Town area. Check out the Toyota Mega Web showroom (free entry) featuring concept cars and driving simulators. Walk along the Odaiba waterfront promenade with views of Rainbow Bridge.
day_by_day.evening: Catch the sunset and evening lights over Tokyo Bay from the Odaiba beachfront. The Rainbow Bridge and Tokyo skyline light up beautifully at dusk. Take the Yurikamome automated monorail back — a scenic elevated ride over the bay.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or convenience store — ¥400
meals.lunch: Odaiba food court at DiverCity — ramen or curry for ¥800–¥1,000
meals.dinner: Odaiba Decks Tokyo Beach food hall — try okonomiyaki or takoyaki for ¥900–¥1,300

day_by_day.notes: The Yurikamome monorail offers great views and is covered by your IC card. Odaiba is a great showcase of Japanese tech culture and futuristic urban planning.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Harajuku — visit Takeshita Street for quirky youth fashion, crepes, and pop culture (free to walk). Then walk through Omotesando for upscale architecture window shopping.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Meiji Shrine (free entry) set in a forested park — a peaceful contrast to the city bustle. Walk the grand torii gate path through the forest. Nearby Yoyogi Park is free and great for people-watching on weekends.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Shibuya for the famous Shibuya Crossing experience. Watch the scramble crossing from the Starbucks overlooking it (buy a coffee for the view — ¥500). Walk the Shibuya Center-gai pedestrian street.

meals.breakfast: Harajuku crepe from a Takeshita Street stall — ¥500–¥700
meals.lunch: Standing sushi bar in Harajuku or Omotesando — ¥1,000–¥1,500
meals.dinner: Shibuya izakaya (Japanese pub) — all-you-can-drink sets and small plates for ¥1,500–¥2,000

day_by_day.notes: Meiji Shrine is free and tranquil. Harajuku and Shibuya are very walkable and connected. Shibuya Crossing is most impressive in the evening with neon lights.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Shinjuku — explore Kabukicho entertainment district in the morning when it's calm and photogenic. Walk through Memory Lane (Omoide Yokocho) — a narrow alley of tiny yakitori stalls (best visited in the evening but atmospheric in the morning too).
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building in Shinjuku for a FREE observation deck with panoramic city views (open daily, free). Explore Shinjuku Gyoen National Garden (¥500 entry) — one of Tokyo's best parks with late-blooming cherry blossoms in April.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Omoide Yokocho (Memory Lane) for dinner — tiny smoky yakitori stalls serving grilled skewers under ¥200 each. This is an iconic budget Tokyo dining experience.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store or nearby bakery in Shinjuku — ¥400–¥600
meals.lunch: Shinjuku ramen alley — a bowl of rich ramen for ¥800–¥1,000
meals.dinner: Omoide Yokocho yakitori — budget ¥1,200–¥1,800 for skewers and a beer

day_by_day.notes: The free Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building observation deck is one of the best free views in the city — go on a clear day. Shinjuku Gyoen may still have late cherry blossoms in mid-April.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Akihabara for deeper tech culture exploration — visit the Akihabara Radio Kaikan building (8 floors of anime, manga, and tech goods). Browse retro Famicom and PC-98 shops. Visit a Gundam Cafe or Super Potato retro game shop.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the nearby Kanda and Jimbocho neighborhood — Tokyo's famous second-hand bookstore district. Hundreds of shops selling old books, manga, maps, and prints. Very budget-friendly browsing.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Ikebukuro — another major tech and otaku culture hub. Visit Sunshine City shopping complex and the Namco entertainment floors. Walk the neon streets of Ikebukuro East Exit.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store — ¥400
meals.lunch: Akihabara curry restaurant — Japanese curry rice for ¥700–¥900
meals.dinner: Ikebukuro ramen — try a tsukemen (dipping ramen) for ¥900–¥1,100

day_by_day.notes: Jimbocho is a hidden gem for book lovers and collectors. Many shops have English-language manga and vintage Japanese prints at low prices. Great for unique souvenirs.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Yanaka — one of Tokyo's best-preserved old-town neighborhoods. Walk Yanaka Ginza shopping street for traditional snacks, crafts, and local life. Explore the historic Yanaka Cemetery (free, beautiful in spring).
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to nearby Nezu Shrine (free) — a smaller, less-crowded alternative to Fushimi Inari with torii gate tunnels. Then explore the Nezu and Yanesen area's traditional wooden buildings and small temples.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Ueno for the evening. Visit Ueno Park (free) and the surrounding area. Browse the cheap restaurants and izakayas near Ueno station.

meals.breakfast: Yanaka Ginza street food — menchi katsu (fried meat cutlet) for ¥200–¥300
meals.lunch: Local teishoku (set meal) restaurant in Yanaka — ¥800–¥1,000
meals.dinner: Ueno izakaya — sashimi platter and drinks for ¥1,500–¥2,000

day_by_day.notes: Yanaka is one of the most authentic and least touristy neighborhoods in Tokyo. Perfect for experiencing everyday local life. Very walkable and free to explore.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the National Museum of Emerging Science and Innovation (Miraikan) on Odaiba — entry ¥630. This is Tokyo's premier science and tech museum featuring robots, space tech, and interactive exhibits. A must for tech culture enthusiasts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Miraikan — don't miss the ASIMO robot demonstrations and the giant globe display. Afterward, visit the adjacent Fuji TV Building observation deck (¥700) for panoramic bay views.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Shiodome's Caretta building and the Shimbashi area for evening. Visit the cheap izakayas and standing bars (tachinomi) around Shimbashi station — a favorite spot for Tokyo salarymen.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or convenience store — ¥400
meals.lunch: Miraikan museum cafe or nearby convenience store — ¥700–¥900
meals.dinner: Shimbashi standing bar (tachinomi) — drinks and small plates for ¥1,000–¥1,500

day_by_day.notes: Miraikan is one of the best tech culture experiences in Tokyo. Book tickets online in advance if possible. The ASIMO robot show times are posted at the entrance.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Nakameguro — a trendy neighborhood along the Meguro River canal. Walk the canal-side path lined with cherry trees (beautiful even after peak bloom). Browse independent cafes, vintage clothing shops, and design stores.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the train to Shimokitazawa — Tokyo's bohemian neighborhood known for vintage shops, live music venues, and indie cafes. Browse the many second-hand clothing and record stores. Free to explore.
day_by_day.evening: Stay in Shimokitazawa for dinner and evening atmosphere. Check out a small live music venue (entry ¥1,000–¥2,000) for local indie bands — this is a great local cultural experience.

meals.breakfast: Nakameguro independent cafe — coffee and toast for ¥600–¥800
meals.lunch: Shimokitazawa curry shop — Japanese or Indian-style curry for ¥800–¥1,000
meals.dinner: Shimokitazawa izakaya or ramen shop — ¥900–¥1,300

day_by_day.notes: Shimokitazawa is one of Tokyo's most authentic local neighborhoods. Very different from tourist areas — great for experiencing real Tokyo youth culture. Many vintage items available at low prices.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Tokyo National Museum in Ueno (¥1,000 entry) — the largest museum in Japan with extensive collections of Japanese art, samurai armor, and cultural artifacts. Budget 2–3 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the rest of Ueno Museum Park (free to walk). Visit the Shinobazu Pond and the surrounding park area. Then head to nearby Yanaka or Nezu for a final stroll through traditional Tokyo streets.
day_by_day.evening: Final big night out in Tokyo — head to Shinjuku or Shibuya for a memorable evening. Visit a rooftop bar for city views, enjoy street food, and soak in the neon atmosphere. Pick up last-minute snacks and souvenirs from a convenience store.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store or hotel — ¥400
meals.lunch: Ueno museum restaurant or nearby teishoku set — ¥900–¥1,200
meals.dinner: Shinjuku or Shibuya izakaya farewell dinner — splurge slightly at ¥2,000–¥2,500 for a memorable last meal

day_by_day.notes: Consider picking up omiyage (souvenir snacks) at a depachika (department store basement food hall) in Shinjuku or Shibuya. These make excellent and affordable gifts. Stock up on instant ramen and snacks at a 100-yen shop.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early and enjoy a final convenience store breakfast. Do a last walk around your hotel neighborhood. Pack and check out. Head to the airport via train or limousine bus — allow at least 2–3 hours before your flight.
day_by_day.afternoon: At the airport, browse duty-free shops for last-minute gifts. Many Japanese snacks and cosmetics are well-priced at airport shops. Return your IC card at the airport for a refund of remaining balance (minus a ¥220 handling fee).
day_by_day.evening: Depart Tokyo. Reflect on 13 amazing days of local food, tech culture, and budget adventures across one of the world's greatest cities.

meals.breakfast: Final convenience store breakfast — onigiri and canned coffee for ¥400
meals.lunch: Airport ramen or soba restaurant — ¥1,000–¥1,500
meals.dinner: On the flight

day_by_day.notes: Return your Suica/Pasmo IC card at the airport Green Windows for a balance refund. Keep your last ¥500–¥1,000 in cash for any last transport needs. Arrive at the airport at least 2.5 hours before international departure.

trip_options.title: Classic Tokyo Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

experiences.name: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore the bustling Tsukiji Outer Market, sampling fresh sushi, tamagoyaki, grilled seafood skewers, and matcha treats from local vendors. Engage with longtime vendors and discover the heart of Tokyo's culinary culture in one of the world's most famous food markets.

experiences.name: Akihabara Electric Town Tech & Anime Immersion
experiences.description: Dive deep into Tokyo's legendary tech and otaku culture in Akihabara. Browse multi-story electronics shops, retro game arcades, robot cafes, and cutting-edge gadget stores. Visit Yodobashi Camera and independent shops selling rare components, vintage consoles, and the latest tech innovations.

experiences.name: Ramen Alley Crawl in Shinjuku
experiences.description: Navigate the narrow lanes of Shinjuku's famous Omoide Yokocho (Memory Lane) and nearby ramen shops to taste regional ramen styles including tonkotsu, shoyu, and miso. Chat with ramen masters who have perfected their broths over decades and experience the authentic izakaya atmosphere.

day_by_day.morning: N/A – In transit. Flight UA arrives at 22:30.
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A – In transit.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Narita/Haneda Airport at 22:30. Clear customs and immigration, collect luggage, and take the airport limousine bus or Narita Express to central Tokyo. Check in to Aegean Bliss Resort. Do a quick convenience store run at a nearby 7-Eleven or FamilyMart for snacks and essentials.

meals.breakfast: Meal on the plane.
meals.lunch: Meal on the plane.
meals.dinner: Grab onigiri, sandwiches, or hot food from a convenience store near the hotel after check-in – a quintessential Tokyo late-night experience.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light. Set your watch to JST (UTC+9). Hydrate well and try to sleep at a local hour to beat jet lag. Prepare your IC card (Suica or Pasmo) at the airport for easy transit throughout the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Ease into Tokyo with a leisurely walk around your hotel neighborhood. Visit a nearby local kissaten (traditional Japanese coffee shop) for a morning set. Then head to Hamarikyu Gardens for a peaceful stroll amid cherry blossom aftermath and seasonal spring flowers, with views of the Tokyo skyline.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the subway to Tsukiji Outer Market for the 'Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour' experience. Browse the stalls, sample fresh sushi, tamagoyaki, grilled seafood skewers, and pick up Japanese snacks. Explore the surrounding Tsukiji neighborhood and peek into specialty food shops.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Ginza for an evening window-shopping stroll along one of Tokyo's most elegant boulevards. Enjoy dinner at a mid-range sushi restaurant or a standing sushi bar in the area for an authentic experience without the high-end price tag.

meals.breakfast: Morning set (toast, egg, coffee) at a local kissaten – approx. ¥500–¥800.
meals.lunch: Tsukiji Outer Market tastings – budget ¥1,500–¥2,500 across multiple stalls for sushi, tamagoyaki, and grilled scallops.
meals.dinner: Standing sushi bar or casual sushi restaurant in Ginza – approx. ¥2,000–¥3,500 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Tsukiji Outer Market is busiest in the morning; arriving by midday still gives great access to most stalls. Wear comfortable walking shoes. Bring cash as many stalls are cash-only.

day_by_day.morning: Head to Akihabara for the 'Akihabara Electric Town Tech & Anime Immersion' experience. Start with multi-story electronics shops like Yodobashi Camera and BIC Camera. Explore retro game shops, figure stores, and the latest gadgets. Visit the AKB48 Theater building and browse maid café menus.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Akihabara – dive into specialty stores like Super Potato for retro gaming, Animate for anime merchandise, and Radio Kaikan for collectibles. Visit a maid café for a uniquely Tokyo cultural experience (budget ¥1,000–¥1,500 for a drink and performance).
day_by_day.evening: Stay in the Akihabara/Ueno area for dinner. Try Kanda Yabu Soba, a historic soba restaurant nearby, or explore the izakayas around Ueno for a lively Friday night atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or grab a pastry and coffee from a local bakery chain like Vie de France near Akihabara station.
meals.lunch: Akihabara area ramen or curry shop – approx. ¥900–¥1,500. Try CoCo Ichibanya for Japanese curry.
meals.dinner: Izakaya dinner in Ueno or Akihabara – approx. ¥2,000–¥3,500 per person with drinks.

day_by_day.notes: Akihabara is most vibrant on weekends but Friday evenings are lively too. Many electronics stores close around 20:00–21:00. Budget extra for tech and anime shopping – it's easy to overspend here!

day_by_day.morning: Visit Senso-ji Temple in Asakusa early morning to beat the weekend crowds. Walk through Nakamise Shopping Street for traditional souvenirs and snacks like ningyo-yaki and age-manju. Explore the surrounding Asakusa neighborhood with its old-Tokyo shitamachi atmosphere.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cross the Azuma Bridge and head to the Sumida River area. Visit the Tokyo Skytree for panoramic city views (mid-range ticket for the Tembo Deck at 350m – approx. ¥2,100). Browse the Solamachi shopping complex at the base of Skytree for local food products and design goods.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Shinjuku for the 'Ramen Alley Crawl' experience. Navigate Omoide Yokocho (Memory Lane) with its tiny yakitori stalls and smoky atmosphere, then explore nearby ramen shops for a rich tonkotsu or shoyu bowl.

meals.breakfast: Age-manju (fried sweet bun) and green tea from a stall in Nakamise Shopping Street – approx. ¥300–¥500.
meals.lunch: Solamachi food hall at Tokyo Skytree – try ekiben (station bento) style meals or Japanese fast food – approx. ¥1,200–¥2,000.
meals.dinner: Omoide Yokocho yakitori skewers and ramen in Shinjuku – approx. ¥2,500–¥3,500 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Senso-ji is open 24/7 but the market stalls open around 10:00. Book Tokyo Skytree tickets online in advance on weekends to avoid long queues. Omoide Yokocho is tiny and smoky – great for atmosphere but not ideal if sensitive to smoke.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Harajuku – start with Takeshita Street for quirky fashion, crepes, and youth culture. Then walk through Omotesando, Tokyo's tree-lined luxury boulevard, for architecture and window shopping at flagship stores.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Meiji Jingu Shrine set within a forested urban sanctuary – a peaceful contrast to the busy streets nearby. Afterward, head to Shibuya to witness the famous Shibuya Scramble Crossing. Visit the Shibuya Sky observation deck for a stunning aerial view of the crossing.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Shibuya. Try Ichiran Ramen for a solo-booth ramen experience, or explore the restaurant floors of Shibuya Hikarie or Shibuya 109 for diverse mid-range dining options.

meals.breakfast: Harajuku crepe from Marion Crepes or Angel Heart – approx. ¥600–¥900.
meals.lunch: Casual café or bento from a depachika (department store basement food hall) in Omotesando – approx. ¥1,200–¥2,000.
meals.dinner: Ichiran Ramen or a restaurant in Shibuya Hikarie – approx. ¥1,500–¥2,800.

day_by_day.notes: Shibuya Sky observation deck tickets should be booked online in advance – approx. ¥2,000. Sunday afternoons in Harajuku and Shibuya are very busy. The Meiji Shrine forest walk takes about 30–40 minutes round trip and is a lovely decompression from city buzz.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Odaiba, Tokyo's futuristic man-made island. Take the driverless Yurikamome Line for scenic bay views. Visit teamLab Borderless or teamLab Planets for an immersive digital art experience (book tickets in advance – approx. ¥3,200).
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Odaiba's tech and pop culture scene – visit DiverCity Tokyo Plaza (home to a life-size Gundam statue), the Miraikan National Museum of Emerging Science and Innovation (approx. ¥630 entry), and browse the Palette Town shopping area.
day_by_day.evening: Return to central Tokyo. Dinner in Shiodome or Shimbashi area – try a local izakaya popular with Tokyo office workers for an authentic salaryman dining experience.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or convenience store breakfast before heading to Odaiba.
meals.lunch: Aqua City Odaiba food court or one of the themed restaurants on the island – approx. ¥1,200–¥2,000.
meals.dinner: Shimbashi izakaya – approx. ¥2,500–¥3,500 per person with drinks.

day_by_day.notes: Book teamLab tickets well in advance as they sell out quickly. The Yurikamome Line offers great views of Rainbow Bridge and Tokyo Bay. Odaiba is very walkable once you're on the island – comfortable shoes recommended.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Yanaka, one of Tokyo's best-preserved old neighborhoods. Walk through Yanaka Cemetery (beautiful in spring), browse the Yanaka Ginza shotengai (old-fashioned shopping street), and discover artisan workshops and local cafés.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Ueno for the Tokyo National Museum (approx. ¥1,000 entry) – Japan's largest museum featuring samurai armor, ukiyo-e woodblock prints, and ancient artifacts. Stroll through Ueno Park and visit Shinobazu Pond.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Ueno or Nezu area. Try a local tonkatsu restaurant or a traditional teishoku (set meal) restaurant for a balanced, home-style Japanese dinner.

meals.breakfast: Coffee and pastry at a local Yanaka café – approx. ¥500–¥800.
meals.lunch: Yanaka Ginza street food – menchi-katsu (fried minced meat cutlet), croquettes, and local snacks – approx. ¥800–¥1,200.
meals.dinner: Tonkatsu or teishoku set meal restaurant in Ueno – approx. ¥1,500–¥2,500.

day_by_day.notes: Yanaka is a wonderful off-the-beaten-path neighborhood that feels like stepping back in time. Many small shops are closed on Tuesdays – check ahead. This is a great day to slow down and soak in local Tokyo life.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Shinjuku Gyoen National Garden for a morning of tranquility – one of Tokyo's finest parks with French, English, and Japanese garden sections (entry approx. ¥500). Ideal for spring greenery and relaxation.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore East Shinjuku – visit Kabukicho entertainment district during daylight for a look at Tokyo's famous nightlife district without the crowds. Then check out the new Godzilla head atop Shinjuku Toho Cinema and browse the Shinjuku Golden Gai area.
day_by_day.evening: Experience the Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building's free observation deck for night views of the city skyline (open until 23:00 on some nights, free entry). Then dinner in the lively Nishi-Shinjuku area.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a morning set at Doutor Coffee near Shinjuku station.
meals.lunch: Shinjuku Takashimaya Times Square depachika lunch – try soba, tempura, or bento options – approx. ¥1,000–¥1,800.
meals.dinner: Izakaya or yakiniku (grilled meat) restaurant in Shinjuku – approx. ¥2,500–¥4,000 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Shinjuku Gyoen prohibits alcohol and is best visited in the morning for peaceful enjoyment. The Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building observation deck is free – a great budget-friendly alternative to paid observation decks. Check opening hours as they vary.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Nikko (approx. 2 hours by Tobu Nikko Line from Asakusa – budget ¥1,360 one way or use a Tobu Pass). Visit the ornate Tosho-gu Shrine, a UNESCO World Heritage Site surrounded by cedar forests and elaborate carvings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Nikko – visit Rinnoji Temple, Futarasan Shrine, and walk along the cedar-lined Omotesando approach. If time allows, stroll to Shinkyo Bridge, the famous red lacquered bridge over the Daiya River.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Tokyo by early evening. Light dinner near the hotel or pick up a Nikko specialty souvenir snack (yuba – tofu skin – is a local delicacy) for the journey back.

meals.breakfast: Grab a convenience store bento or onigiri for the train journey.
meals.lunch: Yuba (tofu skin) cuisine set meal at a Nikko restaurant – approx. ¥1,500–¥2,500.
meals.dinner: Light meal near the hotel – ramen, soba, or convenience store – approx. ¥800–¥1,500.

day_by_day.notes: Purchase the Tobu Nikko All Area Pass for unlimited bus rides within Nikko (approx. ¥2,000) to save on getting between sites. Nikko's main shrines charge separate entry fees (approx. ¥1,300 combined). Start early to make the most of the day trip.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Roppongi for its world-class art museums. Start with the Mori Art Museum in Roppongi Hills (approx. ¥2,000) featuring contemporary international and Japanese art, plus the Tokyo City View observation deck included in the ticket.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the National Art Center, Tokyo in Roppongi (free entry to permanent collection areas, special exhibitions approx. ¥1,500) – one of Japan's largest exhibition spaces with a striking wave-shaped glass façade. Browse the Roppongi Hills complex for design shops and people-watching.
day_by_day.evening: Roppongi transforms at night – explore the restaurant and bar scene. Try a mid-range Japanese-Western fusion restaurant or a standing bar for a Friday night out in one of Tokyo's most international neighborhoods.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or café in the Roppongi Hills complex.
meals.lunch: Roppongi Hills restaurant floors – try a Japanese set lunch (teishoku) for great value – approx. ¥1,000–¥1,800.
meals.dinner: Mid-range restaurant in Roppongi – Japanese-French fusion or teppanyaki – approx. ¥3,000–¥4,500 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Roppongi Art Triangle (Mori Art Museum, National Art Center, Suntory Museum of Art) can be explored over the full day. Friday evenings in Roppongi are lively – perfect for experiencing Tokyo's international nightlife scene if desired.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Koenji and Shimokitazawa – two of Tokyo's hippest neighborhood gems. Start in Koenji for vintage clothing shops, indie record stores, and local coffee culture. Browse the covered shopping arcades (shotengai) for unique finds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Shimokitazawa (15 minutes by Keio Inokashira Line) – explore the bohemian neighborhood known for live music venues, second-hand bookshops, craft beer bars, and independent cafés. Visit the Bonus Track open-air market space.
day_by_day.evening: Stay in Shimokitazawa for dinner and a live music experience at one of the neighborhood's famous small live houses (shimokita is Tokyo's indie music hub). Check listings for evening performances.

meals.breakfast: Local kissaten (traditional Japanese coffee shop) in Koenji – morning set approx. ¥500–¥800.
meals.lunch: Shimokitazawa café or casual restaurant – curry, pasta, or Japanese fusion – approx. ¥1,000–¥1,800.
meals.dinner: Shimokitazawa izakaya or craft beer pub with food – approx. ¥2,500–¥3,500 per person.

day_by_day.notes: These neighborhoods are best explored slowly without a fixed agenda. Saturday is ideal for Shimokitazawa as the Bonus Track market and many pop-up events run on weekends. Bring cash for vintage shops. Live music tickets at small venues are typically ¥1,500–¥3,000 at the door.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Tsukishima neighborhood for monjayaki (Tokyo's savory pancake specialty). Explore Tsukishima's Monja Street – a charming old downtown area. Then head to nearby Kiyosumi-Shirakawa, Tokyo's specialty coffee district, for a world-class third-wave coffee experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the trendy Kiyosumi-Shirakawa and Fukagawa area – visit the Fukagawa Edo Museum (approx. ¥400) for a fascinating recreation of Edo-period Tokyo life. Browse local design shops and galleries in this up-and-coming creative district.
day_by_day.evening: Final big dinner in Tokyo – head to Shinjuku or Ginza for a celebratory meal. Treat yourself to a full omakase sushi experience at a mid-range sushi counter (approx. ¥5,000–¥8,000 per person) or a shabu-shabu/sukiyaki restaurant for a memorable last dinner.

meals.breakfast: Third-wave specialty coffee and pastry in Kiyosumi-Shirakawa – approx. ¥800–¥1,200.
meals.lunch: Monjayaki lunch on Tsukishima's Monja Street – cook at the table, approx. ¥1,500–¥2,500 per person.
meals.dinner: Celebratory omakase sushi or shabu-shabu in Ginza or Shinjuku – approx. ¥5,000–¥8,000 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Kiyosumi-Shirakawa is home to roasters like Allpress Espresso and Kiyosumi Coffee Factory. Monjayaki is a must-try Tokyo-specific dish – staff at Tsukishima restaurants will help you cook it if it's your first time. Book the dinner restaurant in advance on a Sunday.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Tokyo – pack and check out of Aegean Bliss Resort. Take a last walk through the hotel neighborhood for a final coffee and breakfast. Do any last-minute souvenir shopping at a nearby department store basement (depachika) for food gifts to bring home.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the airport with plenty of time. Allow 2–3 hours before departure for check-in, immigration, and security. Browse the airport duty-free shops for last-minute Japanese snacks, sake, cosmetics, and electronics. Enjoy a final Japanese meal at the airport.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Tokyo. Safe travels!

meals.breakfast: Final Tokyo breakfast at a local kissaten or hotel – savor a last Japanese morning set.
meals.lunch: Airport terminal restaurant – try a ramen or soba shop inside the terminal for a proper last Japanese meal – approx. ¥1,200–¥2,000.
meals.dinner: In-flight meal.

day_by_day.notes: Check airport transfer time carefully – Narita Airport requires 60–90 minutes from central Tokyo, Haneda is 30–45 minutes. Keep ¥3,000–¥5,000 yen in cash for airport transport and last expenses. Return or top up your Suica/Pasmo card at the airport. Declare any food items for customs on arrival back home.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Tokyo Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore the bustling Tsukiji Outer Market, sampling fresh sushi, tamagoyaki, grilled seafood skewers, and matcha treats from local vendors. Engage with longtime vendors and discover the heart of Tokyo's culinary culture in one of the world's most famous food markets.

experiences.name: Akihabara Electric Town Tech & Anime Immersion
experiences.description: Dive deep into Tokyo's legendary tech and otaku culture in Akihabara. Browse multi-story electronics shops, retro game arcades, robot cafes, and cutting-edge gadget stores. Visit Yodobashi Camera and independent shops selling rare components, vintage consoles, and the latest tech innovations.

experiences.name: Ramen Alley Crawl in Shinjuku
experiences.description: Navigate the narrow lanes of Shinjuku's famous Omoide Yokocho (Memory Lane) and nearby ramen shops to taste regional ramen styles including tonkotsu, shoyu, and miso. Chat with ramen masters who have perfected their broths over decades and experience the authentic izakaya atmosphere.

experiences.name: teamLab Borderless Digital Art Museum
experiences.description: Experience the world-renowned teamLab Borderless, an immersive digital art museum that blends technology, art, and nature into breathtaking interactive installations. Wander through rooms of flowing light, digital waterfalls, and AI-driven environments that respond to your movement — a perfect fusion of tech culture and creativity.

experiences.name: Depachika Gourmet Basement Food Hall Experience
experiences.description: Descend into the legendary basement food halls (depachika) of Isetan or Takashimaya department stores in Shinjuku. Sample artisan wagashi sweets, premium bento boxes, regional Japanese delicacies, and gourmet street food prepared by top chefs. A uniquely Japanese culinary institution that reflects the country's obsession with food quality and presentation.

day_by_day.morning: N/A – In transit. Flight UA arrives at 22:30. Allow 60–90 minutes for immigration, baggage claim, and customs at Narita/Haneda.
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A – In transit.
day_by_day.evening: Private airport transfer arranged by Aegean Bliss Resort concierge picks you up curbside. Settle into your Beachfront suite, unwind with a welcome amenity, and do a light room-service order before bed. No sightseeing scheduled tonight.

meals.breakfast: On board the flight
meals.lunch: On board the flight
meals.dinner: In-room dining at Aegean Bliss Resort – request the Japanese kaiseki late-night set or a light ramen bowl from the 24-hour menu

day_by_day.notes: Ask the concierge to confirm all upcoming reservations tonight or first thing tomorrow. Store valuables in the in-room safe and set an early alarm for Day 2.

day_by_day.morning: Gentle recovery morning. Enjoy a leisurely breakfast at the resort's signature restaurant overlooking the waterfront. Afterward, take a slow stroll along the beachfront promenade to acclimate to the time zone and fresh spring air. Pick up a pocket Wi-Fi or SIM card from the concierge desk.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depachika Gourmet Basement Food Hall Experience at Isetan Shinjuku or Takashimaya. A private food guide leads you through the legendary underground halls, curating tastings of wagyu sushi bites, premium matcha confections, artisan pickles, and seasonal wagashi. Perfect low-intensity introduction to Tokyo's food culture.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at a Michelin-starred tempura counter in Ginza (e.g., Kondo or Mikawa Zezankyo) – reserve omakase tempura with seasonal vegetables and live seafood. Return to the resort by private car.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast buffet or à la carte – fresh fruit, Japanese tamago, miso soup, and premium coffee
meals.lunch: Tastings within the depachika halls – curated bites count as a gourmet lunch experience
meals.dinner: Omakase tempura at a Michelin-starred Ginza counter – budget ¥25,000–¥35,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: Jet lag may still be a factor – keep the day relaxed and avoid overloading the schedule. Stay hydrated and walk at a comfortable pace.

day_by_day.morning: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour. Arrive by 8:00 AM for a private guided walk through the iconic outer market. Sample ultra-fresh nigiri sushi straight from the vendor, golden tamagoyaki rolled to order, grilled scallop skewers, and seasonal uni. Visit a premium dashi shop and a specialty knife store.
day_by_day.afternoon: From Tsukiji, head to teamLab Borderless Digital Art Museum (pre-booked premium time slot). Spend 2–3 hours wandering through the immersive, boundary-dissolving digital installations where light, sound, and technology merge. A perfect intersection of Tokyo's tech and art identity.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Narisawa in Minami-Aoyama – one of Asia's finest restaurants blending French technique with Japanese 'Innovative Satoyama' philosophy. Book the full tasting menu. Return to the resort by private car.

meals.breakfast: Tastings at Tsukiji Outer Market serve as a substantial breakfast – sushi, tamagoyaki, and fresh seafood
meals.lunch: Light café lunch near teamLab venue – try a premium bento or onigiri from a high-end convenience deli
meals.dinner: Narisawa tasting menu – budget ¥35,000–¥50,000 per person; wine pairing available

day_by_day.notes: teamLab Borderless requires advance timed-entry tickets – book at least 2 weeks ahead. Wear comfortable shoes; both venues involve significant walking.

day_by_day.morning: Akihabara Electric Town Tech & Anime Immersion. Arrive at Akihabara by 10:00 AM with a private tech-culture guide. Explore multi-story electronics megastores (Yodobashi Camera, Sofmap), visit curated retro game shops, and tour the latest robotics and gadget floors. Experience a high-end audiophile listening room.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue in Akihabara with a visit to a premium figure and collectibles gallery, then stop at a maid café for a cultural experience (upscale version available). Transition to Ueno Park for a leisurely cherry blossom walk (mid-April bloom may still be active) and a visit to the Tokyo National Museum.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Sushi Yoshitake in Ginza – a 3-Michelin-star sushi omakase counter. Only 10 seats; intimate and extraordinary. Chef Masahiro Yoshitake sources the finest seasonal fish daily.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast – Japanese set with grilled fish, rice, miso, and pickles
meals.lunch: Akihabara lunch at a high-end curry or tonkatsu restaurant – try Maisen Tonkatsu or a premium Japanese curry house
meals.dinner: Sushi Yoshitake omakase – budget ¥40,000–¥60,000 per person; sake pairing recommended

day_by_day.notes: Akihabara is busiest on weekends – arrive early to avoid crowds. The guide can access private collector showrooms not open to general public.

day_by_day.morning: Private tea ceremony and wagashi-making workshop in a traditional machiya townhouse in Yanaka, Tokyo's best-preserved old neighborhood. Learn the philosophy of wabi-sabi, practice matcha preparation, and hand-craft seasonal wagashi sweets with a master confectioner.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Yanaka Ginza shopping street and the historic cemetery park. Then transfer to Harajuku for a visit to Omotesando – Tokyo's luxury boulevard. Browse flagship stores of Japanese designers (Issey Miyake, Comme des Garçons) and international maisons in their architecturally stunning Tokyo outposts.
day_by_day.evening: Ramen Alley Crawl in Shinjuku. A private guide leads you through Omoide Yokocho (Memory Lane) for yakitori and smoky izakaya bites, then on to three curated ramen shops for comparative tastings – tonkotsu, shoyu, and a truffle-infused luxury ramen. Atmospheric and unforgettable.

meals.breakfast: Light resort breakfast before the tea ceremony
meals.lunch: Traditional kaiseki bento served as part of the tea ceremony experience, or a premium soba lunch in Yanaka
meals.dinner: Ramen Alley Crawl in Shinjuku – multiple tastings across Memory Lane and premium ramen counters; budget ¥8,000–¥15,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: Yanaka is best explored on foot – wear comfortable shoes. The ramen crawl ends late; arrange a private car pickup from Shinjuku for the return to the resort.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day excursion to Nikko (2 hours by private car or shinkansen). Visit the UNESCO World Heritage Tosho-gu Shrine complex, with its ornate carvings, towering cedar forests, and the sacred Yomeimon Gate. Explore the serene Rinno-ji Temple and Futarasan Shrine.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Nikko – walk to Kegon Waterfall and Lake Chuzenji for stunning mountain scenery. Enjoy the fresh mountain air and dramatic spring landscape. Stop at a local Nikko yuba (tofu skin) shop for a tasting.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Tokyo by private car. Quiet dinner at the resort's fine-dining restaurant or a nearby high-end Japanese restaurant to rest after the excursion.

meals.breakfast: Early resort breakfast before departure
meals.lunch: Premium kaiseki lunch at Nikko Kanaya Hotel – a historic luxury hotel dating to 1873, serving refined Japanese-Western fusion
meals.dinner: Resort restaurant or a neighborhood kaiseki – budget ¥20,000–¥30,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: Depart by 7:30 AM to maximize time in Nikko. The private car service allows flexible timing at each site. Book Nikko Kanaya Hotel lunch in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Private sushi masterclass with a former Tsukiji sushi chef. Learn to select fish, prepare shari (sushi rice), and nigiri technique in a professional kitchen. You'll prepare and eat your own omakase breakfast/brunch – an extraordinarily exclusive experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Mori Art Museum in Roppongi Hills for a world-class contemporary art exhibition, then ascend to the Tokyo City View observation deck for panoramic views of the metropolis. Explore the Roppongi Hills complex and its outdoor sculpture garden.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Quintessence in Shirokanedai – a 3-Michelin-star French-Japanese restaurant by Chef Shuzo Kishida, known for his philosophical approach to cuisine. Exceptional wine cellar.

meals.breakfast: Sushi you prepare yourself during the morning masterclass – the ultimate premium breakfast
meals.lunch: Light café or patisserie in Roppongi Hills – try a premium crêpe or seasonal parfait
meals.dinner: Quintessence tasting menu – budget ¥40,000–¥55,000 per person; sommelier-guided wine pairing available

day_by_day.notes: The sushi masterclass requires advance booking (minimum 2 weeks). Maximum 4 participants for an intimate experience. Quintessence requires reservations months in advance – book before the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Tsukishima and Kiyosumi-Shirakawa neighborhood walk. Start with specialty third-wave coffee at Allpress Espresso or Blue Bottle Coffee's flagship Tokyo roastery. Then explore Tsukishima's famous monjayaki (Tokyo-style savory pancake) street and the waterfront.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private guided visit to the Sony Innovation Museum (Sony Park or Sony Showroom in Ginza) and the Panasonic Shiodome Museum. Explore cutting-edge consumer tech, AI robotics demonstrations, and interactive product labs. A deep dive into Japan's tech legacy and future vision.
day_by_day.evening: Kaiseki dinner at Kikunoi Akasaka – a celebrated 3-Michelin-star kaiseki restaurant. Chef Murata's seasonal menu reflects the finest of Japanese culinary philosophy. Private room available for groups.

meals.breakfast: Third-wave coffee and artisan pastry at Blue Bottle Coffee Kiyosumi-Shirakawa flagship
meals.lunch: Monjayaki experience on Tsukishima's Monja Street – try the premium crab and cheese variety
meals.dinner: Kikunoi Akasaka kaiseki – budget ¥30,000–¥45,000 per person; sake pairing curated by the sommelier

day_by_day.notes: Kiyosumi-Shirakawa is a charming, less-touristy neighborhood – great for photography. Book Kikunoi private dining room for an elevated experience.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Kamakura (1 hour by private car). Visit the Great Buddha (Kotoku-in), Engaku-ji Zen temple complex, and the bamboo grove at Hokoku-ji Temple. Participate in a private Zen meditation session with a resident monk at Engaku-ji.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Komachi-dori shopping street in Kamakura for artisan crafts, local sweets, and ceramics. Visit Tsurugaoka Hachimangu Shrine and its cherry blossom-lined approach. Walk the scenic cliffside Daibutsu Hiking Trail.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Tokyo. Dinner at Sushi Saito in Minato (if a reservation miracle occurs) or alternatively at Harutaka in Ginza – both are elite 3-Michelin-star sushi counters offering the pinnacle of Edomae sushi.

meals.breakfast: Early resort breakfast before departure
meals.lunch: Premium seafood lunch at Hachinoki Kitakamakura – a renowned tofu and kaiseki restaurant near Engaku-ji
meals.dinner: Elite Edomae sushi omakase – budget ¥45,000–¥70,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: Sushi Saito is notoriously difficult to book – have the concierge attempt months in advance. Harutaka is an excellent alternative and slightly more accessible. Kamakura is best visited on weekdays to avoid weekend crowds.

day_by_day.morning: Shibuya and Daikanyama exploration. Start at Shibuya Sky observation deck for morning views of the famous scramble crossing. Walk to the architecturally stunning Daikanyama T-Site (Tsutaya Books) – a temple to curated culture, design books, and premium lifestyle.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private tour of a Japanese tech startup hub or innovation lab in Shibuya or Ebisu (arranged by concierge). Meet with founders and engineers working on AI, robotics, or smart city technology. Alternatively, visit the interactive NTT InterCommunication Center in Shinjuku for digital art and tech installations.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Florilège in Aoyama – a 2-Michelin-star progressive French restaurant by Chef Hiroyasu Kawate, celebrated for its open kitchen theater and sustainable philosophy. One of Tokyo's most exciting dining experiences.

meals.breakfast: Specialty coffee and premium pastry at Daikanyama Log Road café or Ivy Place
meals.lunch: Premium lunch at a Daikanyama bistro – try IVY PLACE or Tableaux for French-Japanese fusion
meals.dinner: Florilège tasting menu – budget ¥25,000–¥35,000 per person; natural wine pairing available

day_by_day.notes: Daikanyama T-Site opens at 7:00 AM – arrive early for a peaceful browse before crowds. The tech startup tour requires advance arrangement through the concierge or a Tokyo innovation network contact.

day_by_day.morning: Private traditional indigo dyeing (aizome) workshop in Asakusa with a master artisan. Create your own tenugui (hand towel) or furoshiki (wrapping cloth) using centuries-old techniques. Afterward, explore Nakamise-dori shopping street and Senso-ji Temple complex in the golden morning light.
day_by_day.afternoon: Sumida River private yakatabune (traditional wooden boat) cruise. Drift past the Tokyo Skytree, Rainbow Bridge, and Odaiba waterfront while enjoying seasonal scenery. Premium sake and seasonal snacks served on board. Disembark at Hamarikyu Gardens for a stroll through the tidal garden.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Den in Jimbocho – a creative, playful 2-Michelin-star Japanese restaurant by Chef Zaiyu Hasegawa. Famous for 'Dentucky Fried Chicken' and whimsical seasonal menus that surprise and delight.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at a traditional Asakusa kissaten (old-school coffee shop) – try Pelican Café for toast and coffee
meals.lunch: Premium bento and sake on the yakatabune cruise – freshly prepared seasonal Japanese cuisine
meals.dinner: Den tasting menu – budget ¥25,000–¥35,000 per person; natural wine and sake pairing available

day_by_day.notes: Yakatabune cruises should be booked 1–2 weeks in advance. The Asakusa workshop produces a keepsake to take home. Den requires advance reservation – book 1–2 months ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Luxury spa morning at the resort or a premium onsen facility. Book a full 3-hour ryokan-style treatment: traditional shiatsu massage, hinoki wood bath, and a facial using Japanese botanical ingredients. Complete rest and rejuvenation before the final full day.
day_by_day.afternoon: Final Tokyo shopping experience. Visit the Ginza Six luxury complex for high-end Japanese and international brands. Stop at the Ginza Itoya flagship stationery store (12 floors of Japanese design). Browse Matsuya Ginza's curated artisan craft floor for premium omiyage (gifts) – lacquerware, ceramics, and confections.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at Joël Robuchon Tokyo in Ebisu – the legendary French master's Tokyo outpost, housed in a stunning château. The grand tasting menu with sommelier-guided wine pairing is a fitting luxurious conclusion to the trip.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast – full Japanese-Western spread with premium juice bar
meals.lunch: Ginza Six rooftop restaurant or a premium sushi lunch at a Ginza counter – try Sushi Iwa or Sushi Umi
meals.dinner: Joël Robuchon Tokyo grand tasting menu – budget ¥50,000–¥80,000 per person; Champagne and wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Pack purchased items carefully tonight. Prepare luggage for the departure tomorrow. The concierge can arrange professional luggage packing or shipping service (takkyubin) to the airport.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning at leisure. Enjoy a slow resort breakfast with ocean views. Take one last walk along the beachfront promenade. Visit the hotel gift shop for any remaining omiyage. Check out by 11:00 AM (late checkout may be arranged with concierge).
day_by_day.afternoon: Private airport transfer departs the resort. Arrive at the airport 3 hours before international departure. Access the premium international lounge (JAL Sakura Lounge or ANA Suite Lounge at Haneda, or the United Club at Narita) for a final Japanese meal, shower, and relaxation before boarding.
day_by_day.evening: Departure. Carry warm memories of 13 extraordinary days in Tokyo.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely final resort breakfast – order your favorite dishes from the trip
meals.lunch: Premium airport lounge dining – Japanese noodles, seasonal bento, and sake
meals.dinner: On board or at the departure lounge

day_by_day.notes: Confirm airport transfer time with concierge the night before. Duty-free shopping at the airport is excellent for last-minute whisky, cosmetics, and snacks. Keep receipts for tax refund processing at the airport customs counter.
